dedupe_keys.name: chemm case studies in chemical incident response hhs aspr

description: This collection presents detailed case studies of large chemical emergencies to draw lessons for future responses, covering interagency coordination, evacuation and shelter-in-place decisions, medical management of casualties and responder safety. The studies shown on the page read are the organic peroxide fires at the Arkema plant in Crosby, Texas, in August 2017, the vinyl chloride release after the Norfolk Southern derailment in February 2023, the hydrogen sulfide release at the PEMEX Deer Park refinery near Houston in October 2024, which killed two people, injured over 35 and led to a shelter-in-place order, and the Novichok poisoning in Salisbury, England, in 2018. It is published by the Chemical Hazards Emergency Medical Management (CHEMM) site of the US Department of Health and Human Services' preparedness office. Coverage is mainly US incidents, and the filter also lists chlorine, hydrocyanic acid, methyl isocyanate and sarin. The studies are free online and can be printed or downloaded; no licence is stated. Caveats: the site notes it is under construction, and the studies are narrative accounts, not data. For simulation it gives reference events for modelling toxic releases from plants and transport, evacuation and hospital surge, and for testing emergency response plans around chemical sites. It is related to the Natech H2S release case study record in this catalogue, a modelled release from a process plant.
